topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: nouns, pronouns and determiners
points: Forming feminine and plural nouns; infinitives used as nouns; names of languages and nationality nouns
Articles: agreement, functions, contractions del and al
Demonstrative adjectives (este, ese; aquel (HT)); indefinite and possessive adjectives
Subject pronouns and their default omission; algo and alguien
Direct and indirect object pronouns and word order; reflexive pronouns
Relative pronouns que, lo que, el que, el cual; relative clauses with cuando, donde (HT)
Possessive pronouns; neuter aquello, esto, eso; interrogative pronouns (HT)
Alguno and ninguno as pronouns; pronouns after prepositions, conmigo, contigo (HT)

topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: verbs and tenses
points: Negation: no, nada, nunca, nadie, ninguno; ya no, tampoco, ni…ni (HT)
Interrogatives: intonation, question words and word order
Passive voice: ser + past participle + por; se + 3rd person
Impersonal verbs: hay, hay que, se puede, hace + noun; parece, basta, falta, hace falta, vale la pena (HT)
Reflexive verbs and interesar-type verbs
Acabar de + infinitive; seguir and llevar + present participle
Modal verbs: deber, poder, querer, saber, tener que; quisiera and me gustaría + infinitive
Present tense: regular, stem-changing and irregular verbs; desde hace + present (HT)
Present continuous and imperfect continuous
Perfect tense (haber + past participle)
Preterite: regular and irregular forms; spelling and -ir stem changes (HT)
Imperfect tense (plural forms and ser, ir, ver (HT))
Periphrastic future (ir a + infinitive) and inflectional future
Conditional tense
Affirmative imperative (tú; plural forms (HT))
Present subjunctive and its uses after cuando, wishing/emotion, que, para que (HT)

topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: adjectives, adverbs, prepositions and pronunciation
points: Adjectives: agreement in gender and number, nationality adjectives, position (buen, gran etc.)
Adjectives (HT): possessives after verbs, meaning change by position, neuter lo + adjective
Comparative and superlative adjectives (mejor, peor, el mejor)
Adverbs: position; comparative and superlative adverbial structures
Prepositions: personal a, de for possession, para/sin/antes de/después de + infinitive, prepositions in questions
Derivational morphology: -ito/-ita, -ísimo/-ísima, -mente, -idad, -able
Sound-symbol correspondences for read aloud and dictation; stress patterns and written accents (HT)

Task 3: broader conversation

Section B: dictation

topics.name: Paper 3 Reading

Section B: translation from Spanish into English (Foundation 5 sentences, Higher a passage)

topics.name: Paper 4 Writing
points: Foundation Q1: picture-based task (four short sentences)
Formal open response (Foundation 40 to 50 words; Higher 130 to 150 words)
Informal open response (80 to 90 words)
Translation from English into Spanish (Foundation 5 sentences, Higher a short paragraph)
